sanskrit: vadaty anīśam ātmānaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭro mahīpatiḥ āpṛcche bhavataḥ sarvān gamiṣyāmi yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the lord of the earth, declaring himself powerless, takes leave of all of you — I shall go to Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: āmantrya prasthitaṃ śauriṃ rathasthaṃ puruṣarṣabham anujagmur maheṣvāsāḥ pravīrā bharatarṣabhāḥ
english: Having bidden farewell to Śauri as he set out, mounted on his chariot — that bull among men — the great archers, the heroic bulls of the Bhārata line, followed after him.

sanskrit: bhīṣmo droṇaḥ kṛpaḥ kṣattā dhṛtarāṣṭro 'tha bāhlikaḥ aśvatthāmā vikarṇaś ca yuyutsuś ca mahārathaḥ
english: Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, Vidura, and then Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Bāhlika, Aśvatthāmā, Vikarṇa, and the great chariot-warrior Yuyutsu.

sanskrit: tato rathena śubhreṇa mahatā kiṅkiṇīkinā kurūṇāṃ paśyatāṃ prāyāt pṛthāṃ draṣṭuṃ pitṛṣvasām
english: Then, on a splendid great chariot adorned with small bells, while the Kurus watched, he departed to visit Pṛthā, his father's sister.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca praviśyātha gṛhaṃ tasyāś caraṇāv abhivādya ca ācakhyau tat samāsena yad vṛttaṃ kurusaṃsadi
english: Vaishampаyana said: Entering her house and touching her feet in reverence, he told her in brief all that had transpired in the Kuru assembly.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca uktaṃ bahuvidhaṃ vākyaṃ grahaṇīyaṃ sahetukam ṛṣibhiś ca mayā caiva na cāsau tad gṛhītavān
english: Vāsudeva said: Many kinds of words worthy of acceptance, with sound reasons, were spoken both by the sages and by me — yet he did not take them to heart.

sanskrit: kālapakvam idaṃ sarvaṃ duryodhanavaśānugam āpṛcche bhavatīṃ śīghraṃ prayāsye pāṇḍavān prati
english: All of this has been ripened by Time and follows the will of Duryodhana. I take leave of you now — I shall swiftly set out toward the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: kiṃ vācyāḥ pāṇḍaveyās te bhavatyā vacanān mayā tad brūhi tvaṃ mahāprājñe śuśrūṣe vacanaṃ tava
english: What shall I say to those sons of Pāṇḍu on your behalf? Tell me, O greatly wise one — I am eager to hear your words.

sanskrit: kunty uvāca brūyāḥ keśava rājānaṃ dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram bhūyāṃs te hīyate dharmo mā putraka vṛthā kṛthāḥ
english: Kuntī said: Say to the king Yudhiṣṭhira, whose soul is dharma, O Keśava: "Your dharma diminishes ever more — do not act in vain, my son."

sanskrit: śrotriyasyeva te rājan mandakasyāvipaścitaḥ anuvākahatā buddhir dharmam evaikam īkṣate
english: Like that of a dull and ignorant student of scripture, O king, your intellect, dulled by mere recitation, sees only one aspect of dharma.

sanskrit: aṅgāvekṣasva dharmaṃ tvaṃ yathā sṛṣṭaḥ svayaṃbhuvā urastaḥ kṣatriyaḥ sṛṣṭo bāhuvīryopajīvitā krūrāya karmaṇe nityaṃ prajānāṃ paripālane
english: Contemplate dharma in its entirety — as the Self-born One created it: the Kṣatriya was created chest-first, to live by the strength of his arms, for fierce action and for the constant protection of his subjects.

sanskrit: śṛṇu cātropamām ekāṃ yā vṛddhebhyaḥ śrutā mayā mucukundasya rājarṣer adadāt pṛthivīm imām purā vaiśravaṇaḥ prīto na cāsau tāṃ gṛhītavān
english: Hear also this one illustration which I have heard from the elders: Vaiśravaṇa, pleased of old, offered this very earth to the royal sage Mucukunda — yet he did not accept it.

sanskrit: bāhuvīryārjitaṃ rājyam aśnīyām iti kāmaye tato vaiśravaṇaḥ prīto vismitaḥ samapadyata
english: "I desire to enjoy a kingdom won by the strength of my own arms" — at this, Vaiśravaṇa was delighted and filled with wonder.

sanskrit: mucukundas tato rājā so 'nvaśāsad vasuṃdharām bāhuvīryārjitāṃ samyak kṣatradharmam anuvrataḥ
english: Then King Mucukunda duly governed the earth, won by the strength of his arms, steadfastly devoted to the dharma of the Kṣatriya.

sanskrit: yaṃ hi dharmaṃ carantīha prajā rājñā surakṣitāḥ caturthaṃ tasya dharmasya rājā bhārata vindati
english: Of whatever dharma the subjects practice here, well protected by the king, the king, O Bhārata, obtains a fourth share of that merit.

sanskrit: rājā carati ced dharmaṃ devatvāyaiva kalpate sa ced adharmaṃ carati narakāyaiva gacchati
english: If the king practices dharma, he qualifies for divinity; if he practices adharma, he goes straight to hell.

sanskrit: daṇḍanītiḥ svadharmeṇa cāturvarṇyaṃ niyacchati prayuktā svāminā samyag adharmebhyaś ca yacchati
english: The science of punishment, wielded according to its own dharma, holds the four social orders in check; properly applied by the master, it restrains them from adharma as well.

sanskrit: daṇḍanītyāṃ yadā rājā samyak kārtsnyena vartate tadā kṛtayugaṃ nāma kālaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ pravartate
english: When the king acts fully and properly according to the science of punishment, then the best of ages, known as the Kṛta Yuga, comes into being.

sanskrit: kālo vā kāraṇaṃ rājño rājā vā kālakāraṇam iti te saṃśayo mā bhūd rājā kālasya kāraṇam
english: Whether Time is the cause of the king, or the king is the cause of Time — let there be no doubt in your mind: the king is the cause of Time.

sanskrit: rājā kṛtayugasraṣṭā tretāyā dvāparasya ca yugasya ca caturthasya rājā bhavati kāraṇam
english: The king is the creator of the Kṛta Yuga and of the Tretā; the king is the cause of the Dvāpara and also of the fourth age.

sanskrit: kṛtasya kāraṇād rājā svargam atyantam aśnute tretāyāḥ kāraṇād rājā svargaṃ nātyantam aśnute pravartanād dvāparasya yathābhāgam upāśnute
english: By being the cause of the Kṛta, the king enjoys heaven permanently; by being the cause of the Tretā, the king does not enjoy heaven permanently; from bringing about the Dvāpara, he enjoys it in proportion to his share.

sanskrit: tato vasati duṣkarmā narake śāśvatīḥ samāḥ rājadoṣeṇa hi jagat spṛśyate jagataḥ sa ca
english: Thereafter the evildoer dwells in hell for eternal years; for the world is touched by the king's fault, and he in turn is touched by the world's.

sanskrit: rājadharmān avekṣasva pitṛpaitāmahocitān naitad rājarṣivṛttaṃ hi yatra tvaṃ sthātum icchasi
english: Attend to the royal dharmas befitting your fathers and grandfathers — for the position in which you wish to remain is not the conduct of a royal sage.

sanskrit: na hi vaiklavyasaṃsṛṣṭa ānṛśaṃsye vyavasthitaḥ prajāpālanasaṃbhūtaṃ kiṃ cit prāpa phalaṃ nṛpaḥ
english: A king who is joined to feebleness and established in compassion obtains no fruit whatsoever that arises from the protection of his subjects.

sanskrit: na hy etām āśiṣaṃ pāṇḍur na cāhaṃ na pitāmahaḥ prayuktavantaḥ pūrvaṃ te yayā carasi medhayā
english: For neither Pāṇḍu, nor I, nor your grandfather ever previously employed that wisdom by which you now conduct yourself.

sanskrit: yajño dānaṃ tapaḥ śauryaṃ prajāsaṃtānam eva ca māhātmyaṃ balam ojaś ca nityam āśaṃsitaṃ mayā
english: Sacrifice, giving, austerity, valor, and the continuance of progeny, as well as magnanimity, strength, and vigor — these I always wished for you.

sanskrit: nityaṃ svāhā svadhā nityaṃ dadur mānuṣadevatāḥ dīrgham āyur dhanaṃ putrān samyag ārādhitāḥ śubhāḥ
english: The deities among men always offer the svaha and svadha oblations; when properly worshipped, the auspicious ones bestow long life, wealth, and sons.

sanskrit: putreṣv āśāsate nityaṃ pitaro daivatāni ca dānam adhyayanaṃ yajñaṃ prajānāṃ paripālanam
english: The ancestors and the gods ever hope for from their sons: giving, study of scripture, sacrifice, and the protection of subjects.

sanskrit: etad dharmam adharmaṃ vā janmanaivābhyajāyathāḥ te stha vaidyāḥ kule jātā avṛttyā tāta pīḍitāḥ
english: Whether this is dharma or adharma, you were born into it from birth itself; you are skilled, born in a noble family, yet afflicted by want of proper livelihood, my son.

sanskrit: yat tu dānapatiṃ śūraṃ kṣudhitāḥ pṛthivīcarāḥ prāpya tṛptāḥ pratiṣṭhante dharmaḥ ko 'bhyadhikas tataḥ
english: When wanderers of the earth, hungry, find a lord of giving who is a hero, and go away satisfied — what dharma is higher than that?

sanskrit: dānenānyaṃ balenānyaṃ tathā sūnṛtayāparam sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyād rājyaṃ prāpyeha dhārmikaḥ
english: By giving he wins some, by strength he wins others, by gentle truth yet others — the righteous man, having obtained a kingdom here, should receive tribute from all sides.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaḥ pracared bhaikṣaṃ kṣatriyaḥ paripālayet vaiśyo dhanārjanaṃ kuryāc chūdraḥ paricarec ca tān
english: A Brahmin should go about begging alms; a Kṣatriya should protect; a Vaiśya should earn wealth; a Śūdra should serve all of them.

sanskrit: bhaikṣaṃ vipratiṣiddhaṃ te kṛṣir naivopapadyate kṣatriyo 'si kṣatāt trātā bāhuvīryopajīvitā
english: Begging is forbidden to you; agriculture does not suit you either; you are a Kṣatriya — one who protects from harm, who lives by the strength of his arms.

sanskrit: pitryam aṃśaṃ mahābāho nimagnaṃ punar uddhara sāmnā dānena bhedena daṇḍenātha nayena ca
english: O mighty-armed one, retrieve again your paternal inheritance that has been submerged — by conciliation, by giving, by creating dissension, by force, or by statecraft.

sanskrit: ito duḥkhataraṃ kiṃ nu yad ahaṃ hīnabāndhavā parapiṇḍam udīkṣāmi tvāṃ sūtvāmitranandana
english: What could be more painful than this — that I, bereft of kinsmen, having borne you, O joy of enemies, now look on while you depend on another's food?

sanskrit: yudhyasva rājadharmeṇa mā nimajjīḥ pitāmahān mā gamaḥ kṣīṇapuṇyas tvaṃ sānujaḥ pāpikāṃ gatim
english: Fight according to royal dharma; do not drown your ancestors; do not go, you and your younger brothers, your merit exhausted, to a sinful destiny.

sanskrit: kunty uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam vidurāyāś ca saṃvādaṃ putrasya ca paraṃtapa
english: Kuntī said: In this connection, O scorcher of foes, they also cite this ancient tale — the dialogue between Vidurā and her son.

sanskrit: atra śreyaś ca bhūyaś ca yathā sā vaktum arhati yaśasvinī manyumatī kule jātā vibhāvarī
english: In this matter she speaks of what is truly better and more beneficial, as she deserves — the glorious, indignant Vibhavari, born of a noble family.

sanskrit: kṣatradharmaratā dhanyā vidurā dīrghadarśinī viśrutā rājasaṃsatsu śrutavākyā bahuśrutā
english: Vidurā — blessed, far-sighted, devoted to Kṣatriya dharma — was renowned in royal assemblies, her words heard with attention, a woman of great learning.

sanskrit: vidurā nāma vai satyā jagarhe putram aurasam nirjitaṃ sindhurājena śayānaṃ dīnacetasam anandanam adharmajñaṃ dviṣatāṃ harṣavardhanam
english: The truthful woman named Vidurā indeed rebuked her own son — defeated by the king of Sindhu, lying down with a dejected mind, joyless, ignorant of dharma, a source of delight to his enemies.

sanskrit: na mayā tvaṃ na pitrāsi jātaḥ kvābhyāgato hy asi nirmanyur upaśākhīyaḥ puruṣaḥ klībasādhanaḥ
english: You were born neither of me nor of your father — from where indeed have you come? You are without spirit, a side-branch sort of man, a coward's tool.

sanskrit: yāvajjīvaṃ nirāśo 'si kalyāṇāya dhuraṃ vaha mātmānam avamanyasva mainam alpena bībharaḥ manaḥ kṛtvā sukalyāṇaṃ mā bhais tvaṃ pratisaṃstabha
english: If you are without hope of good fortune for as long as you live, then bear the yoke; do not demean yourself, do not support yourself on so little — set your mind on full well-being, do not be afraid; brace yourself.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha he kāpuruṣa mā śeṣvaivaṃ parājitaḥ amitrān nandayan sarvān nirmāno bandhuśokadaḥ
english: Rise up, O coward — do not lie like this, defeated, gladdening all your enemies, without honor, causing grief to your kinsmen.

sanskrit: supūrā vai kunadikā supūro mūṣikāñjaliḥ susaṃtoṣaḥ kāpuruṣaḥ svalpakenāpi tuṣyati
english: A small stream is easily filled; a mouse's cupped paws are easily filled; a coward is easily satisfied — he is content with very little.

sanskrit: apy arer ārujan daṃṣṭrām āśveva nidhanaṃ vraja api vā saṃśayaṃ prāpya jīvite 'pi parākrama
english: Either wrench out the fang of your enemy and go swiftly to death, or, even when your life hangs in the balance, show valor.

sanskrit: apy areḥ śyenavac chidraṃ paśyes tvaṃ viparikraman vinadan vātha vā tūṣṇīṃ vyomni vāpariśaṅkitaḥ
english: Either watch like a hawk for an opening in your enemy as you move about — calling out or in silence, or unsuspected in the sky above.

sanskrit: tvam evaṃ pretavac cheṣe kasmād vajrahato yathā uttiṣṭha he kāpuruṣa mā śeṣvaivaṃ parājitaḥ
english: Why do you lie like this, like a ghost or one struck by the thunderbolt? Rise up, O coward — do not lie like this, defeated.

sanskrit: māstaṃ gamas tvaṃ kṛpaṇo viśrūyasva svakarmaṇā mā madhye mā jaghanye tvaṃ mādho bhūs tiṣṭha corjitaḥ
english: Do not fall into wretchedness; be known by your own deeds. Do not remain in the middle ranks, nor in the lowest — do not be slack; stand vigorous and strong.

sanskrit: alātaṃ tindukasyeva muhūrtam api vijvala mā tuṣāgnir ivānarciḥ kākaraṅkhā jijīviṣuḥ muhūrtaṃ jvalitaṃ śreyo na tu dhūmāyitaṃ ciram
english: Blaze forth even for a moment, like a firebrand of tinduka wood — do not smolder flameless like a fire of chaff, clinging to life like a crow's wish. To blaze for a moment is better than to smolder with smoke for a long time.

sanskrit: mā ha sma kasya cid gehe janī rājñaḥ kharīmṛduḥ kṛtvā mānuṣyakaṃ karma sṛtvājiṃ yāvad uttamam dharmasyānṛṇyam āpnoti na cātmānaṃ vigarhate
english: In no man's house should a woman born of a king, gentle as a she-ass, live; having performed the human duty and entered battle to the highest degree, one becomes free from the debt of dharma and does not reproach oneself.

sanskrit: alabdhvā yadi vā labdhvā nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ānantaryaṃ cārabhate na prāṇānāṃ dhanāyate
english: Whether they obtain it or not, the wise do not grieve; they undertake action without pause and do not treasure their lives like wealth.

sanskrit: udbhāvayasva vīryaṃ vā tāṃ vā gaccha dhruvāṃ gatim dharmaṃ putrāgrataḥ kṛtvā kiṃnimittaṃ hi jīvasi
english: Either manifest your valor or go to that certain path — with dharma placed before you, my son; for what reason do you live?

sanskrit: iṣṭāpūrtaṃ hi te klība kīrtiś ca sakalā hatā vicchinnaṃ bhogamūlaṃ te kiṃnimittaṃ hi jīvasi
english: Your sacrificial merit and the merit of public works are destroyed, O coward; your entire fame is slain and the root of your enjoyment cut off — for what reason then do you live?

sanskrit: śatrur nimajjatā grāhyo jaṅghāyāṃ prapatiṣyatā viparicchinnamūlo 'pi na viṣīdet kathaṃ cana udyamya dhuram utkarṣed ājāneyakṛtaṃ smaran
english: An enemy who is sinking should be seized by the thigh; one who is about to fall should be grabbed; even one whose roots are entirely severed should not despair in any way — he should lift up the yoke with effort, recalling the acts of a thoroughbred horse.

sanskrit: kuru sattvaṃ ca mānaṃ ca viddhi pauruṣam ātmanaḥ udbhāvaya kulaṃ magnaṃ tvatkṛte svayam eva hi
english: Cultivate courage and self-respect; know your own manliness; raise up your family that has submerged — for it is because of you that it has sunk.

sanskrit: yasya vṛttaṃ na jalpanti mānavā mahad adbhutam rāśivardhanamātraṃ sa naiva strī na punaḥ pumān
english: He whose conduct men do not extol as great and wonderful, who merely adds to his heap — he is neither a woman nor yet a man.

sanskrit: dāne tapasi śaurye ca yasya na prathitaṃ yaśaḥ vidyāyām arthalābhe vā mātur uccāra eva saḥ
english: He whose fame is not spread abroad in giving, in austerity, in valor, or in learning or the gaining of wealth — he is nothing but his mother's excrement.

sanskrit: śrutena tapasā vāpi śriyā vā vikrameṇa vā janān yo 'bhibhavaty anyān karmaṇā hi sa vai pumān
english: He who surpasses other people by learning, by austerity, by prosperity, by valor, or by action — he truly is a man.

sanskrit: na tv eva jālmīṃ kāpālīṃ vṛttim eṣitum arhasi nṛśaṃsyām ayaśasyāṃ ca duḥkhāṃ kāpuruṣocitām
english: But you ought not to seek out the wretched, beggarly mode of life — cruel, inglorious, painful, fit only for cowards.

sanskrit: yam enam abhinandeyur amitrāḥ puruṣaṃ kṛśam lokasya samavajñātaṃ nihīnāśanavāsasam
english: That wretched man whom enemies would welcome — weak, universally despised by the world, in mean food and clothing —

sanskrit: aholābhakaraṃ dīnam alpajīvanam alpakam nedṛśaṃ bandhum āsādya bāndhavaḥ sukham edhate
english: — pitiable, inspiring only the cry "Alas, the wretch!", of little life and little worth — obtaining such a kinsman, no kinsman prospers.

sanskrit: avṛttyaiva vipatsyāmo vayaṃ rāṣṭrāt pravāsitāḥ sarvakāmarasair hīnāḥ sthānabhraṣṭā akiṃcanāḥ
english: We ourselves shall perish from want — exiled from our kingdom, deprived of all the pleasures of desire, fallen from our station, possessing nothing.

sanskrit: avarṇakāriṇaṃ satsu kulavaṃśasya nāśanam kaliṃ putrapravādena saṃjaya tvām ajījanam
english: I bore you, Sañjaya, as a source of reproach among the good, a destroyer of the family line, a discord — and now your name is spoken only in shame.

sanskrit: niramarṣaṃ nirutsāhaṃ nirvīryam arinandanam mā sma sīmantinī kā cij janayet putram īdṛśam
english: Without indignation, without enthusiasm, without valor, a delight to enemies — may no woman with a parting in her hair ever give birth to such a son.

sanskrit: mā dhūmāya jvalātyantam ākramya jahi śātravān jvala mūrdhany amitrāṇāṃ muhūrtam api vā kṣaṇam
english: Do not merely smolder — blaze forth with full intensity; advance and slay your foes; burn on the heads of your enemies even for a moment or an instant.

sanskrit: etāvān eva puruṣo yad amarṣī yad akṣamī kṣamāvān niramarṣaś ca naiva strī na punaḥ pumān
english: A man is a man to precisely this extent: that he is full of indignation and does not endure wrong; one who endures but is without indignation is neither a woman nor yet a man.

sanskrit: saṃtoṣo vai śriyaṃ hanti tathānukrośa eva ca anutthānabhaye cobhe nirīho nāśnute mahat
english: Contentment indeed destroys prosperity, and so does excessive compassion; both the fear of exertion and inertia — the inactive man does not obtain greatness.

sanskrit: ebhyo nikṛtipāpebhyaḥ pramuñcātmānam ātmanā āyasaṃ hṛdayaṃ kṛtvā mṛgayasva punaḥ svakam
english: Free yourself from these sinful evils of baseness by your own will; make your heart like iron and seek again what is your own.

sanskrit: puraṃ viṣahate yasmāt tasmāt puruṣa ucyate tam āhur vyarthanāmānaṃ strīvad ya iha jīvati
english: Because he endures and bears the citadel of the body, he is called a purusha — a man; they say his name is meaningless, like a woman's, who lives thus in this world.

sanskrit: śūrasyorjitasattvasya siṃhavikrāntagāminaḥ diṣṭabhāvaṃ gatasyāpi vighase modate prajā
english: Even the leavings of a hero of vigorous spirit who walks with the stride of a lion — even one who has gone to the fate decreed — his subjects rejoice in those leavings.

sanskrit: ya ātmanaḥ priyasukhe hitvā mṛgayate śriyam amātyānām atho harṣam ādadhāty acireṇa saḥ
english: He who, abandoning his own personal pleasure and ease, seeks prosperity — he quickly brings joy to his ministers.

sanskrit: putra uvāca kiṃ nu te mām apaśyantyāḥ pṛthivyā api sarvayā kim ābharaṇakṛtyaṃ te kiṃ bhogair jīvitena vā
english: The son said: What is the whole earth worth to you who have lost sight of me? What need have you of ornaments, of pleasures, or of life itself?

sanskrit: mātovāca kim adyakānāṃ ye lokā dviṣantas tān avāpnuyuḥ ye tv ādṛtātmanāṃ lokāḥ suhṛdas tān vrajantu naḥ
english: The mother said: May those who are enemies today obtain the worlds of those who are enemies; but may the worlds of those who honor themselves, the worlds of friends, come to us.

sanskrit: bhṛtyair vihīyamānānāṃ parapiṇḍopajīvinām kṛpaṇānām asattvānāṃ mā vṛttim anuvartithāḥ
english: Do not follow the way of life of those abandoned by their servants, who live on another's food — wretched, without spirit.

sanskrit: anu tvāṃ tāta jīvantu brāhmaṇāḥ suhṛdas tathā parjanyam iva bhūtāni devā iva śatakratum
english: May Brahmins and friends live following after you, my son — as living beings follow the rain-cloud, as the gods follow the hundred-sacrificed Indra.

sanskrit: yam ājīvanti puruṣaṃ sarvabhūtāni saṃjaya pakvaṃ drumam ivāsādya tasya jīvitam arthavat
english: The man whom all creatures live by, O Sañjaya — approaching him as they would a ripe tree — his life is full of meaning.

sanskrit: yasya śūrasya vikrāntair edhante bāndhavāḥ sukham tridaśā iva śakrasya sādhu tasyeha jīvitam
english: The hero by whose valorous deeds his kinsmen prosper in happiness — as the thirty gods thrive by Śakra's might — well indeed is his life lived here.

sanskrit: svabāhubalam āśritya yo 'bhyujjīvati mānavaḥ sa loke labhate kīrtiṃ paratra ca śubhāṃ gatim
english: The man who lives and prospers relying on the strength of his own arms — he obtains fame in this world and an auspicious passage in the next.

sanskrit: vidurovāca athaitasyām avasthāyāṃ pauruṣaṃ hātum icchasi nihīnasevitaṃ mārgaṃ gamiṣyasy acirād iva
english: Vidurā said: And yet in this condition you wish to abandon manliness — it seems you will shortly take the path trodden by the low.

sanskrit: yo hi tejo yathāśakti na darśayati vikramāt kṣatriyo jīvitākāṅkṣī stena ity eva taṃ viduḥ
english: For a Kṣatriya who does not display his energy to the full extent of his power through valorous action, yet clings to life — him they know as nothing but a thief.
